questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had friends in Sydney, and a martial arts club I knew that I was going to join before applying, but UNSW's academic and career opportunities definitely cemented my choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNSW is extremely welcoming towards international and exchange students, and organizes a ton of onboarding experiences to ensure students are well integrated into campus life. I quickly made new friends, got comfortable exploring campus, and joined a student club. The courses are well structured, ensuring an organized learning environment, and I got to apply theory in practice, equipping me for a future career setting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The UNSW Abroad & Exchange Team is quick to reply, given that you have been polite and very specific in your enquiries. Additional important information will be provided via email and the UNSW website, including tutorials and valuable information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Airport pickup, email reminders regarding student ID, UNSW student introduction, campus tour, faculty welcome, and O-week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was recommended
flatmates.com.au
, and had a family member who could make sure that the place would not scam me. I was lucky to find accommodation near the campus with nice roommates; however, this may not be the case for everyone else. I know of people who had to move several times to find accommodation that suited their needs, before they finally settled down in Sydney. My general advice would be to stay at a hostel or an Airbnb before settling in to ensure the place's conditions.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of scammers. I recommend finding something close to campus, as it is often cheaper in the long run and saves you time throughout the week. Public transportation in Sydney will be crowded, especially during rush hour, and the fares add up. In my opinion, it's better to go to the beach, etc., on the weekend than to have to sweat over delayed buses and trains. Think about what experience you envision for yourself; do you want to live with international students and improve your English, or do you wanna live with other Danes that provide a sense of comfort and security? Eating out is generally more expensive than cooking at home, but grocery store prices are at a higher price range. You might wanna consider having the option of being able to cook at home.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really lucky with my accommodation. I liked living next to campus, as I had time to prepare breakfast and lunch at a reasonable hour before I had to leave for class. The campus is pretty big. It takes 30+ minutes to walk from the lower campus to the higher campus. Even though I lived next door, I would still have to leave half an hour before class to make sure I arrived on time.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Before enrollment, your courses will be approved through Endeavor. However, once you attempt to enroll in the course on myUNSW, you might receive a message indicating that you need permission to enroll across careers. To resolve this issue, contact the UNSW Abroad & Exchange Team.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: During your exchange application, you will apply for courses through Endeavor. You can read about the specific courses and their requirements via the UNSW Handbook, which will be emailed to you by the UNSW Abroad & Exchange Team. Once your courses have been approved, you can watch a YouTube tutorial on how to register for the courses through myUNSW.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails detailing the necessary steps, including links to tutorials, and online assistance with the UNSW Abroad & Exchange Team.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Browse through the courses and make a backup list, as you will have to apply for extra courses in case the class is fully registered. My favorite course was the one I took to improve my CV rather than for pleasure. I personally did not enjoy the online course I took purely because of it being online, so if you can do all your classes in person, I high recommend doing so.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors and teachers are very knowledgeable, which shines through in their classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As an MA student, you cannot enroll in BA-level courses. The level of courses is high and includes a lot of reading, weekly tests, group work, tutorials, monthly assignments, and exams throughout the trimester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures are structured in a similar format. The tutorials are a mixture of seminars and group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: BEES6601-Sydney Environment (T2 25), LING5003-Language Technology (T3 25), MODL5106-Text Analysis for Translation (T3 25), and LING5015-Discourse Analysis (T3 25).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BEES6601-Sydney Environment (T2 25), if you are interested in Sydney wildlife and want to go on hikes, or have general concerns about spiders, snakes, and sharks. LING5003-Language Technology (T3 25), if you are interested in the current and emerging technologies that will influence the future, e.g., AI, Python, corpus linguistics, translation tools, etc., and how to work with them. MODL5106-Text Analysis for Translation (T3 25), if you plan on working with interpreting or in translations. The course gives you a good foundation of how the industry works, what to think about when translating in practice, and how to apply theory in practice. LING5015-Discourse Analysis (T3 25), if you are interested in linguistics and discourse, and want to develop your transcription abilities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Even if you do not join a club or society, there are still events available during the week on campus or at the Roundhouse.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Go to
https://www.arc.unsw.edu.au/
to read all about the social activities available for students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A sportsclub! It provides a community and makes sure you get in some weekly exercise. I personally recommend Taido.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do a weekend trip to the Blue Mountains, Byron Bay, Jarvis Bay, and Melbourne. For holidays, go to Perth, Tasmania, or Uluru.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australians are very cheerful and will welcome you with open arms. If you look lost, they will offer you help without having to ask. Within a couple of weeks, you've pretty much gotten the hang of things around here in terms of local grocery stores, coffee shops, bars, etc.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club or society, and talk to your classmates during class breaks. Join the events on campus, and go on the guided tours.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not a lot to be fair.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How multicultural Sydney and Australia are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't underestimate the winter and rainy weather. It takes a little while to find your social group, and that is ok, you will find your people here. Get out of your comfort zone, explore the city, and meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: https://www.unsw.edu.au/student

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my overall English proficiency while honing my academic skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time crunch of a trimester. Your schedule will be pretty packed with studying as an MA student, but it will be extremely rewarding in terms of acquired skills and knowledge.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
